title: Deep learning on 12-lead ECGs predicts bloodstream infection in emergency patients
summary: A deep learning model trained on ECGs from adult emergency patients at a Taiwanese center (N = 163,826) predicted clinically significant bloodstream infection with AUCs of 0.821 (internal, n = 22,205), 0.800 (external, n = 22,709) and 0.756 (MIMIC-IV, n = 66,937). The high-risk group had adjusted hazard ratio 3.43 (1.93-6.09) for 90-day mortality among infected patients. The study is retrospective and discrimination is modest; the authors note prospective validation is needed.
ai_technology: Deep learning model on standard 12-lead ECGs
organization: Tri-Service General Hospital, National Defense Medical University

evidence.tested: Three independent test cohorts: internal, external hospital and MIMIC-IV.
evidence.unknown: Prospective performance; pathogen-specific prediction (an exploratory analysis only); full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Estimates bloodstream infection risk from the ECG at emergency presentation.
